elements.title: Figure 5.—Value of Metals and Metallic Minerals Produced in 2023, by Region
elements.content:
Map of the United States divided into four regions: West (red), Midwest (orange), South (light orange), Northeast (cream). Alaska and Hawaii shown in insets, colored red (West). States are labeled with codes representing metals/minerals produced. Explanation legend for value in billion dollars: 0 to 0.3 (cream), >0.3 to 5 (light orange), >5 to 15 (orange), 25 (red).

State codes and metals/minerals:
- Au: Gold
- B1: Copper ± molybdenum ± gold ± silver ± rhenium
- B2: Copper ± silver
- B3: Lead and zinc ± copper ± silver
- B4: Silver ± zinc ± lead ± gold
- B5: Nickel ± copper ± cobalt ± gold
- B6: Cobalt, copper, gold
- B7: Cobalt, copper, nickel
- Be: Beryllium
- Cu: Copper
- Fe: Iron ore
- IRZ: Ilmenite, rutile, and zircon
- Mg: Magnesium
- Mo: Molybdenum
- P1: Silver ± base metals ± gold
- P2: Gold and silver
- P3: Gold and silver ± base metals
- P4: Platinum ± palladium ± gold ± silver
- REE: Rare-earth elements
- Zn: Zinc

Examples of state codes:
- Washington: P2, P1, B1, B6
- California: IRZ, P2, REE
- Arizona: B1, Cu, B2, Cu, B1, Cu, Cu, Cu, B1
- Alaska: B4, Au
- Michigan: B5, Fe
- Tennessee: Zn, Zn, Zn
- Florida: IRZ, IRZ, REE

Regions labeled in white text: West, Midwest, South, Northeast.
elements.notes: Source not explicitly stated on map. Codes explained below map.
